binary_algorithm: Validate profile and finite arguments, then set one monotonic deadline before Popen. Use binary PIPEs and no main-thread stdin write/flush/close. If spawn raises or returns after deadline, preserve that origin, mark closure unknown unless proven, and use the same emergency path; no successful result or later semantic work.

As in8e2, start two daemon readers and one daemon writer. Readers read4096-byte chunks, require bytes, and reject a channel before extending beyond its profile cap. Writer checks the complete byte count and closes stdin in its own finally; any implicit buffered flush remains on that worker, never the caller thread.

Keep the first worker failure code plus monotonic timestamp under a lock, set the shared bad event, and discard later worker messages. At each work check, an observed worker failure within the deadline wins; otherwise expiry gives PROCESS_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. No exception text or raw output enters this latch.

Process wait and every normal work-thread join consume the same remaining work budget with the reviewed <=.05s polling slices. Popen/thread creation/start/join failures are bounded safe origins. Check exit type, all work-thread completion and deadline before accepting normal work.

In finally, create exactly one cleanup_deadline=monotonic()+2 for the entire process cleanup, not2s per stream/action. Use guarded daemon cleanup calls for terminate/kill/pipe closes. Preserve8e2 terminate join<=.25 and short wait<=.25, then kill/wait only if still unexited, each clipped to shared remaining budget. Attempt asynchronous close of all three pipes and join work/cleanup threads only with that remaining budget.

Successful Result additionally requires observed exit, no live work/cleanup thread, no cleanup error, every pipe closed, and no latched worker failure. An earlier primary failure survives terminate/kill/close/join/persistence failures; later closure failures are secondary, sticky and still veto PASS.

Record only safe per-dispatch profile/byte-count/deadline/exit/pipe/thread closure Booleans and fixed codes. Never export process/thread/descriptor handles or raw data. Bound in-memory capture and discard partial buffers on overflow or decoding failure; never parse a truncated prefix as complete evidence.

Exact identity inspection/removal of run-owned resources remains eligible controlled cleanup; evidence stays stopped if transport or cleanup is unconfirmed.
